task_instance: Fetch and address review comments on the open GitHub PR for the current branch using gh CLI (per SKILL.md steps 1-3): run gh auth status, list PR review threads/comments via gh, summarize them, and apply a fix for a user-selected comment.
blocker_detail: The skill's very first prerequisite is an authenticated `gh` CLI session ('ensure gh is authenticated ... run gh auth status with escalated permissions'), and its core deliverable (fetching real PR review comments and pushing fixes back for the user's PR) requires a live, authenticated connection to a real GitHub repository/PR owned by an account. In this sandbox, `gh auth status` reports 'Failed to log in to github.com using token (GH_TOKEN): The token in GH_TOKEN is invalid.' The task rules explicitly forbid searching for or using credentials/tokens and forbid using the github MCP connector tool, and gh CLI access to a real repo is inherently account-bound. Without valid GitHub credentials there is no real open PR to fetch comments from, so scripts/fetch_comments.py (step 1) cannot produce genuine review-thread data, and the whole comment-triage/fix workflow cannot be exercised against a real deliverable. Fabricating a fake local 'PR comments' JSON and running the fix logic against it would not exercise the skill's actual core intent (interacting with a live GitHub PR via authenticated gh), so it was not attempted as a substitute.
evidence: cd into work directory; `which gh` -> /usr/local/bin/gh (present); `gh auth status` -> 'X Failed to log in to github.com using token (GH_TOKEN)' / 'The token in GH_TOKEN is invalid.' No further steps taken since fixing auth would require locating/using credentials, which is explicitly forbidden by the safety rules, and the github MCP tool is also explicitly off-limits.
